name: Programming Basics
description: Variables, types, control flow and functions: the building blocks of every program.

name: Problem Solving & Complexity
description: Break problems into steps and reason about how code scales with Big O.

name: Recursion & Discrete Math
description: Think recursively and learn the discrete math behind algorithms.

name: How Computers Work
description: Boolean logic, binary and hexadecimal, computer architecture and how memory and pointers work.

name: Processes & Memory
description: How the operating system runs processes and threads and manages virtual memory, the stack and the heap.

name: Scheduling, System Calls & Synchronization
description: How the kernel schedules work and serves system calls and I/O, and how locks and semaphores prevent races and deadlocks.

name: Linux & Shell
description: Work comfortably in a Linux shell and understand how file systems organize data.

name: Arrays, Strings & Hashing
description: The everyday data structures: arrays, strings, hash tables and sets.

name: Linked Lists, Stacks & Queues
description: Linear structures and when to reach for a linked list, a stack or a queue.

name: Trees & Heaps
description: Binary trees and heaps, the structures behind hierarchies and priority queues.

name: Search Trees, Tries & String Algorithms
description: Ordered lookups with binary search trees, prefix search with tries and classic string algorithms.

name: Graphs & Traversal
description: Model relationships as graphs and explore them with BFS and DFS.

name: Searching & Sorting
description: Sorting algorithms and binary search, and the trade-offs between them.

name: Two Pointers & Sliding Window
description: Two classic patterns that turn quadratic scans over arrays and strings into linear ones.

name: Matrices & Prefix Sums
description: Work with grids and matrices and answer range queries fast with prefix sums.

name: Tree Traversal & Divide and Conquer
description: Recursive algorithms that split a problem into smaller ones: tree traversals and divide and conquer.

name: Greedy & Intervals
description: Greedy choices and the interval problems, like merging and scheduling, where they shine.

name: Backtracking & Dynamic Programming
description: Search solution spaces with backtracking and avoid repeated work with dynamic programming.

name: Advanced Graph Algorithms
description: Topological sort, shortest paths and union-find for dependency, routing and connectivity problems.

name: Network Models & Transport
description: The OSI and TCP/IP models, IP addressing and subnetting, and TCP versus UDP.

name: DNS & HTTP
description: How names resolve to addresses and how HTTP and HTTPS carry the web.

name: TLS, NAT & Firewalls
description: Encrypt traffic with TLS and certificates, and control it with NAT and firewalls.

name: Proxies, CDNs & WebSockets
description: Proxies and load balancers, CDNs and long-lived WebSocket connections.

name: HTTP & APIs
description: Build REST APIs over HTTP and design them well: resources, status codes, pagination and versioning.

name: Webhooks, Real-Time & gRPC
description: Integration styles beyond request/response: webhooks, WebSockets and SSE, and gRPC.

name: Caching & Queues
description: Speed up services with caching and idempotent APIs, and move slow work to background jobs and queues.

name: Security Foundations
description: The two most exploited web weaknesses: injection and broken access control.

name: Authentication Fundamentals
description: How web apps keep users signed in with sessions, cookies and tokens, and how XSS and CSRF attacks abuse them.

name: Passwords, OAuth & OIDC
description: Store passwords safely, add MFA, and delegate identity with OAuth, OpenID Connect and JWT.

name: API & Infrastructure Security
description: Defend services against SSRF, configure CORS, security headers and TLS, and manage secrets with least privilege.

name: Threat Modeling & Secure Coding
description: Use the OWASP Top 10 and threat modeling to find risks early, and write code that resists them.

name: SQL Foundations
description: Query relational data with SELECT, filtering, sorting and joins.

name: SQL for Analytics
description: Summarize data with GROUP BY and HAVING, and answer harder questions with subqueries, CTEs and window functions.

name: SQL for Applications
description: Keep application data correct with transactions, ACID, isolation levels, locking and MVCC.

name: SQL Performance
description: Read query plans, choose the right indexes and fix N+1 queries and connection pool problems.

name: Data Modeling & Scaling
description: Model data with normalization and constraints, then scale it with replication, sharding, pooling and NoSQL stores.

name: System Design Foundations
description: Client-server basics, caching with Redis and CDNs: the first tools for building fast systems.

name: Scaling Systems
description: Scale vertically and horizontally, balance load and partition data across machines.

name: Messaging & Events
description: Decouple services with queues, message brokers and events, and make consumers idempotent.

name: Rate Limiting & API Gateways
description: Protect and route traffic with rate limiting, API gateways and service discovery.

name: Distributed Systems
description: Resilience patterns, consistency and consensus, and sagas with the outbox pattern for work that spans services.

name: High Availability & Disaster Recovery
description: Design for failure with redundancy across regions and availability zones, and plan disaster recovery.

name: Safe Releases & SLOs
description: Release with blue/green, canary and feature flags, and decide how much risk to take with SLOs and error budgets.

name: Design Trade-offs & Interviews
description: Make and explain technical decisions, communicate architecture and work through classic system design interviews.

name: C# Fundamentals
description: C# syntax, types, structs and records, and object-oriented programming with classes and interfaces.

name: Generics, Collections & LINQ
description: Write reusable typed code with generics, pick the right collection and query it with LINQ.

name: C# Language Features
description: Exceptions and nullable references, delegates and events, and reflection with attributes.

name: Async & Concurrency in C#
description: async/await and tasks, threads, locks and concurrent collections.

name: Memory & Performance in C#
description: The garbage collector and IDisposable, Span<T> and allocation-friendly code.

name: Python Core
description: Pythonic syntax and collections, functions and decorators, iterators and generators, classes and exceptions.

name: Python Tooling & Testing
description: Modules and virtual environments, type hints and automated testing.

name: Python Concurrency & Performance
description: asyncio, threads and processes, and making Python code faster.

name: Java Core
description: Language basics, classes and interfaces, exceptions, generics, collections and streams.

name: JVM, Concurrency & Spring
description: How the JVM and its garbage collector work, threads and concurrency, and Spring fundamentals.

name: JavaScript Core
description: Types and coercion, scope and closures, functions and this, objects, prototypes and classes.

name: Async JavaScript & the DOM
description: Promises, async/await and the event loop, plus the DOM and fetch.

name: Modules, Errors & Performance
description: Organize code with modules, handle errors well and avoid memory and performance pitfalls.

name: TypeScript Basics
description: Primitive types and inference, and when to use interfaces or type aliases.

name: Unions, Generics & Modules
description: Model data with unions and narrowing, write generic code and organize it with enums and modules.

name: Advanced TypeScript Types
description: Utility types and advanced type-level programming.

name: HTML & CSS
description: Semantic HTML and modern CSS layout with Flexbox and Grid.

name: Accessibility & Responsive Design
description: Build interfaces everyone can use, on every screen size.

name: Browser Rendering & Web Performance
description: How browsers render pages and how to make them load and respond fast.

name: Frontend Architecture & Security
description: Structure frontends and their state, and protect them from client-side attacks.

name: React Foundations
description: Components and JSX, props, state and events, and the useState and useEffect hooks.

name: Refs, Context & Custom Hooks
description: Reach the DOM with refs, share state with context and extract logic into custom hooks.

name: Rendering & Memoization
description: How React renders and reconciles, and when useMemo, useCallback and memo actually help.

name: Data Fetching & Forms
description: Fetch and cache server data with React Query and build forms with solid validation.

name: React in Production
description: Routing, error boundaries and testing React components.

name: The .NET Platform
description: The CLR, JIT and GC, dependency injection, and configuration, options and logging.

name: ASP.NET Core
description: Middleware, routing and endpoints, with authentication and authorization.

name: EF Core
description: Map and query data with Entity Framework Core and keep it fast and safe under concurrency.

name: Hosting & Testing .NET
description: Background services and health checks, and testing .NET applications.

name: Testing Essentials
description: Unit tests with Arrange-Act-Assert, then integration and end-to-end tests.

name: Test Doubles & Test Design
description: Isolate code with mocks, stubs and fakes, and design boundary, negative and regression tests.

name: Testing Strategy
description: TDD and the test pyramid, plus property-based, mutation and contract testing.

name: TDD Fundamentals
description: Learn the red-green-refactor cycle, write tests first in small steps and practise it on classic katas.

name: TDD in Practice
description: Use TDD outside-in with test doubles, fix bugs and refactor safely, tame legacy code and avoid the common pitfalls.

steps.title: Bug Fixes & Safe Refactoring with TDD

name: Performance Testing & Profiling
description: Load and stress test systems, then profile and benchmark code to find the bottleneck.

name: CI/CD
description: Turn code into versioned build artifacts and ship them through continuous integration and delivery pipelines.

name: Infrastructure as Code
description: Manage configuration and secrets per environment and provision infrastructure as code with Terraform.

name: Observability Essentials
description: Structured logging and distributed tracing with OpenTelemetry.

name: Metrics & Alerting
description: Measure services with metrics and the golden signals, and turn them into dashboards, alerts and incident response.

name: Docker Essentials
description: What containers are and how images, layers and the build cache work.

name: Dockerfile & Compose
description: Write efficient multi-stage Dockerfiles and run multi-container apps with Docker Compose.

name: Docker in Production
description: Volumes, networks and ports, image registries, and container security and resource limits.

name: Kubernetes Essentials
description: Clusters, nodes and namespaces, and running pods with deployments and ReplicaSets.

name: Kubernetes Networking, Config & Storage
description: Expose workloads with services and ingress, configure them with ConfigMaps and Secrets, and persist data with volumes.

name: Kubernetes in Production
description: Health probes, requests, limits and autoscaling, and rolling updates.

name: Cloud Foundations
description: IaaS, PaaS and SaaS, compute options from VMs to serverless, and managed storage and databases.

name: AWS Foundations
description: The core AWS services, and how cloud identity and secrets keep access under control.

name: Cloud Operations
description: Cloud networking, load balancing and autoscaling, monitoring, and how the same concepts map to Google Cloud.

name: Azure Compute, Data & Identity
description: App Service, Container Apps, Functions and AKS, Azure SQL, PostgreSQL and Blob Storage, and Key Vault with managed identity.

steps.title: App Service, Container Apps, Functions & AKS

name: Azure Messaging, Networking & Monitoring
description: Service Bus and Event Grid, virtual networks and gateways, and Azure Monitor with Application Insights.

steps.title: VNet, Load Balancer, App Gateway & Front Door

name: ML Foundations
description: Supervised and unsupervised learning, training and validation, and the metrics used to judge models.

name: Supervised Models
description: Regression and classification, the bias-variance trade-off and regularization, and tree ensembles.

name: Features, Clustering & Neural Networks
description: Engineer better features, find structure with clustering and PCA, and train neural networks.

name: LLM Application Basics
description: How neural networks, transformers and LLMs work, tokens and context windows, and prompting for structured outputs.

name: RAG & Retrieval
description: Embeddings and vector search, and retrieval-augmented generation with chunking and reranking.

name: Tool Calling & Agents
description: Let models call functions and tools, and build agents with memory and MCP.

name: Production AI
description: Evaluate quality and hallucinations, defend against prompt injection, and manage latency, cost and routing.

name: Data Pipelines
description: ETL and ELT, batch versus streaming, and orchestrating pipelines.

name: Data Storage & Formats
description: Warehouses, lakes and lakehouses, and storing data efficiently with Parquet and partitioning.

name: Kafka & Data Quality
description: Stream events with Kafka and keep data trustworthy with schema evolution and quality checks.

name: Design Principles
description: SOLID, coupling and cohesion, and DRY, KISS and YAGNI.

name: SOLID in Practice
description: Apply the five SOLID principles to real code: spot violations, refactor them and explain the trade-offs in an interview.

name: Design Patterns
description: Creational, structural and behavioral patterns, plus repository and unit of work for data access.

name: Layered & Clean Architecture
description: Layered, clean, hexagonal and onion architectures, and how they keep the domain independent.

name: Monoliths, Microservices & DDD
description: Choose between a modular monolith and microservices, and draw the boundaries with domain-driven design.

name: Event-Driven, CQRS & Serverless
description: Event-driven architecture, CQRS and event sourcing, API gateways and BFFs, and serverless.

name: Git Essentials
description: Repositories and commits, branches, merges and resolving conflicts.

name: Git Collaboration
description: Fetch, pull and push with remotes, and team workflows built on pull requests.

name: Rewriting & Recovering History
description: Rebase, reset and revert, and power tools like cherry-pick, stash and tags.

name: Code Review & Mentoring
description: Give and receive useful code reviews and help teammates grow.

name: Behavioral Interview
description: Answer behavioral questions with the STAR method, talk about mistakes honestly and handle offers and negotiation.

name: Junior Technical Interview
description: The OOP, web and database questions juniors get asked, and how to think aloud while you code.

name: Onboarding & Your First 90 Days
description: Onboard well, read an unfamiliar codebase, ask for help at the right time and turn feedback into a growth plan.

steps.title: Asking for Help & Learning on the Job

name: Pull Requests for Juniors
description: Open small, clear pull requests, take review feedback well and review your teammates' code with confidence.

name: Incidents & Reliability
description: Handle incidents calmly, learn from them and build reliability practices into the team.

name: Statistics Foundations
description: Summarize data with descriptive statistics, reason with probability and distributions, and spot sampling bias.

name: Statistical Inference & Experiments
description: Draw conclusions from samples with hypothesis tests and confidence intervals, tell correlation from causation, run A/B tests and fit simple regressions.

name: Spreadsheets for Analysis
description: Formulas and references, lookups, data validation and cleaning, pivot tables and charts in Excel and Google Sheets.

name: Data Analysis with NumPy & pandas
description: Load, clean, join and aggregate tabular data with NumPy and pandas.

name: Time Series & Reproducible Notebooks
description: Resample and window time-indexed data with pandas, and keep notebook analyses reproducible.

name: Data Visualization
description: Pick the right chart for the question, plot it with Matplotlib and Seaborn, and combine charts into clear dashboards.

name: BI Modeling & Tools
description: Model data for BI and learn the core concepts shared by Power BI, Tableau and Looker.

name: Business Questions & Storytelling
description: Turn business questions into KPIs and metrics, and present findings as a story that drives decisions.

name: AI-Assisted Development
description: Work effectively with coding agents: give them context and instruction files, prompt for code, connect tools with MCP and review what they produce.

name: Claude Code Workflows
description: Scale agent work with subagents and hooks, keep it safe with permissions, control cost and latency, and run agents in CI.

name: AWS Core Services in Depth
description: IAM and least privilege, VPC networking, EC2, containers and Lambda, S3, RDS and DynamoDB, and CloudWatch.

name: C++ Foundations
description: C++ syntax and types, pointers and references, and classes with object-oriented design.

name: Memory, RAII & Move Semantics
description: Manage object lifetimes with RAII and smart pointers, and avoid needless copies with move semantics.

name: Templates, STL & Modern C++
description: Write generic code with templates, use STL containers and algorithms, adopt C++17/20/23 features and build projects with CMake.

name: Concurrency & Undefined Behavior
description: Threads, atomics and the memory model, and how to recognize and avoid undefined behavior such as data races.

name: Security Operations & Incident Response
description: How a SOC detects threats, how teams respond to incidents, and the forensics basics that preserve evidence.

name: Threats, Vulnerabilities & Pentesting
description: Know the malware families, run a vulnerability management program and follow an ethical penetration testing methodology.

name: Cryptography, Zero Trust & Cloud Security
description: Cryptography basics, identity-centric zero trust, securing cloud workloads and the compliance frameworks that audit them.

name: API Security Best Practices
description: Use the OWASP API Security Top 10 to secure authentication and tokens, enforce object- and function-level authorization, and validate input against mass assignment.

name: API Hardening & Monitoring
description: Limit abuse with rate limits, lock down transport, CORS and secrets, and log and monitor APIs to detect attacks.

name: Backend Performance Best Practices
description: Budget latency on hot paths, access data efficiently at scale, cache with a clear invalidation strategy, apply backpressure and trim payloads and round trips.

name: Code Review Best Practices
description: Review with clear goals, keep pull requests small, check correctness, design, tests and security, give useful feedback and automate the rest.

name: AWS Best Practices
description: Apply the Well-Architected Framework: optimize cost, secure accounts and workloads, and design for reliability, backup and disaster recovery.

name: Data Analyst Capstone
description: A scenario-based final challenge mixing spreadsheets, statistics, SQL, pandas, visualization and business storytelling.

name: AI & Data Scientist Capstone
description: A scenario-based final challenge mixing statistics, data wrangling, machine learning, model evaluation and LLMs.

name: AI-Assisted Development Capstone
description: A scenario-based final challenge on planning, steering, securing and reviewing work done with coding agents.

name: Cyber Security Capstone
description: A scenario-based final challenge mixing detection, incident response, vulnerability management, and cloud and API security.

name: C++ Capstone
description: A scenario-based final challenge mixing memory management, RAII, templates, the STL, concurrency and undefined behavior.
